references.text: Here the Sabbath is mentioned as a holy day to be honored, in line with how God blessed and sanctified the seventh day at creation.
God reminds the Israelites of the significance of the Sabbath as a sign between Him and them, and that it is an everlasting covenant based on the rest He established at creation.
Moses repeats the Sabbath commandment in Deuteronomy, but here it is grounded in the deliverance from Egypt, showing that the Sabbath has multiple theological layers beyond the rest of creation.
The author of Hebrews refers to God's rest on the seventh day as a picture of the eternal rest believers will attain through Christ.
Direct quote/allusion confirming God's rest as a theological foundation for the concept of the Sabbath.
The direct legislative explanation of the origin of the Sabbath based on the completion of creation.
Theological elaboration interpreting the rest of creation as a prophetic precursor to an eternal Sabbath rest for God's people.
